summary.text: Sandy Rosenberg is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 41 who was first elected in 1982 and has served since 1983, and he is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.

An attorney and adjunct law professor, he serves on the Health Committee, where he chairs the Health Occupations Subcommittee, and is House chair of the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review.

paragraphs.text: Sandy Rosenberg, whose formal name is Samuel I. Rosenberg, was born in Baltimore on May 18, 1950, and graduated from Baltimore City College, according to his General Assembly biography.
He earned a B.A. in political science from Amherst College in 1972 and a J.D. from Columbia University Law School in 1975.

Before and during his legislative career he worked as a producer at WJZ-TV, a program administrator at the Housing Authority of Baltimore City, and executive director of the Homeless Persons Representation Project, and he has been an adjunct professor at the University of Baltimore and University of Maryland law schools since 1990.
Rosenberg served on the Appropriations Committee from 1983 to 2003, was vice chair of the Judiciary Committee from 2004 to 2011, and was vice chair of the Ways and Means Committee from 2011 to 2013.

He sat on the Judiciary Committee from 2013 to 2017 and on the Health and Government Operations Committee from 2017 to 2025, and he has been House chair of the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review since 2013.
His biography lists the Maryland Access to Justice Commission's Legislator of the Year award in 2012 and the House of Delegates' Casper R. Taylor, Jr. Founder's Award in 2016.
Ballotpedia reports that he advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.
